detail:
The Office on Women's Health describes PMDD as similar to premenstrual syndrome but more serious, causing severe irritability, depression, or anxiety in the week or two before a period starts, with symptoms usually going away two to three days after the period starts. The office notes that diagnosis involves a health history, a physical examination, and a calendar or diary of symptoms, and that five or more symptoms, including one mood-related symptom, are part of the diagnostic picture it describes.

For treatment, the office describes antidepressants in the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) class, noting that the FDA has approved medicines in this class for PMDD, and a hormonal birth control pill approved by the FDA to treat PMDD symptoms. The source also describes over-the-counter pain relievers for physical symptoms such as cramps and headaches, stress management approaches, and general healthy changes as part of the picture, while noting that PMDD can be serious enough to warrant clinician discussion of treatment options.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about managing premenstrual dysphoric disorder.
summary: The Office on Women's Health describes PMDD management including SSRI-class antidepressants and an FDA-approved hormonal contraceptive option, alongside symptom tracking for diagnosis and clinician discussion of treatment.
takeaways: symptom calendars and diaries are part of diagnosis, the office notes
treatments described include SSRI-class medicines and a hormonal contraceptive option
never start, stop, or change medicines without your doctor
title: PMDD (Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder): treatments described by the Office on Women's Health
